The hidden-genetic-variation option is wrong because clones are genetically identical, and every plant within a treatment has the same color. The no-effect option is wrong because aluminum uptake differs strongly among the treatments and color changes with pH.

s3-bio-31.stem: A print shop copies a two-strip master scroll as described in the table. The shop owner uses the table as a model of DNA replication at a replication fork. Which statement correctly connects a feature of the model to the process it represents and makes a correct prediction from the table's numbers?

stimulus.description: Table matching parts of a print-shop model for copying a two-sheet master scroll to parts of DNA replication at one replication fork, with model rules and measurements.

data.title: Print-shop model of copying a two-strand master scroll
rows: Two strips taped together; the strips are pulled apart just ahead of the copier
Can only print by moving in one direction along a strip (toward the open end where strips are separating) for the strip it faces in that direction
Strip B (copier must move away from the opening)
Copied in separate short segments; each segment starts with a small sticker label that is later removed, gaps are filled, and segments are taped together
One original strip plus one newly printed strip
Window of strip pulled apart in this trial
Length of each short segment on Strip B

options.text: Strip B's short segments represent Okazaki fragments made on the lagging strand; the 1,200-unit window needs 6 segments, and no labels are needed because DNA polymerase starts chains alone.
options.why: Misconception: DNA polymerase can initiate a new strand without a primer; ignores the model's labels, which stand for RNA primers.

options.text: Strip B's short segments represent Okazaki fragments made on the lagging strand; the 1,200-unit window needs 6 segments, each started by a removable label like an RNA primer.
options.why: Correct: segments are Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand, 1200/200 = 6, and the removable sticker labels model RNA primers that are later replaced and joined by ligase.

options.text: Each finished copy being one original strip plus one new strip shows conservative replication, in which the original scroll stays intact and a fully new scroll is made.
options.why: Misconception: confusing semiconservative with conservative replication; each copy being one old plus one new strip is semiconservative, not conservative.

options.text: Strip A's continuous run represents the lagging strand, so the 1,200-unit window needs 1 segment on Strip A and 6 on Strip B, each started by a label.
options.why: Misconception: reversing leading and lagging strands; the continuous run is the leading strand, and the discontinuous synthesis is the lagging strand.

s3-bio-31.explanation_en: The strip copied in short segments corresponds to the lagging strand, whose fragments (Okazaki fragments) arise because DNA polymerase synthesizes only 5' to 3' and so must work away from the fork. With 1,200 units open and 200-unit segments, 1200/200 = 6 fragments are needed. The removable labels model RNA primers, which are needed to start each fragment and are later replaced and sealed by ligase. The option claiming no labels are needed is wrong because DNA polymerase cannot start a chain without a primer. The option describing the original scroll staying intact is wrong because one old strip plus one new strip per copy is semiconservative replication. The option assigning the continuous run to the lagging strand is wrong because the continuously copied strip is the leading strand.

s3-bio-32.stem: In a cell-free translation experiment, a ribosome is stopped at the stage shown in the diagram. The next tRNA binds the A site, and a peptide bond then forms. Which model of the next steps correctly represents the relationship among mRNA, tRNA, and the growing polypeptide?

stimulus.description: Diagram of a ribosome on a synthetic mRNA (5' to 3'): AUG CCA GUU UAA. The P site is over AUG and holds a tRNA with anticodon 3'-UAC-5' carrying methionine. The A site is empty and positioned over CCA. A table lists the codon meanings.

data.direction_of_ribosome_movement: toward the 3' end of the mRNA

options.text: A tRNA with anticodon 3'-GGU-5' carrying Pro binds the A site, and Pro is transferred onto Met, so the Met-Pro chain remains attached to the tRNA in the P site.
options.why: Misconception: the new amino acid is added to the P-site tRNA; in fact the growing chain moves to the A-site tRNA.

options.text: A tRNA with anticodon 3'-CCA-5' carrying Pro binds the A site, and Met is transferred onto Pro, so the Met-Pro chain is attached to the tRNA in the A site.
options.why: Misconception: the anticodon is identical to the codon rather than complementary to it.

options.text: A tRNA with anticodon 3'-GGU-5' carrying Pro binds the A site, and Met is transferred onto Pro, so the Met-Pro chain is attached to the tRNA in the A site.
options.why: Correct: the anticodon is complementary and antiparallel to CCA (3'-GGU-5'), the tRNA carries Pro per the codon table, and the peptidyl group is transferred from the P-site tRNA to the amino acid on the A-site tRNA.

options.text: A tRNA with anticodon 3'-GGU-5' carrying Val binds the A site, and Met is transferred onto Val, so the Met-Val chain is attached to the tRNA in the A site.
options.why: Misconception: the tRNA is chosen by the following codon (GUU) rather than the codon currently in the A site (CCA), and the anticodon is mismatched to the amino acid.

s3-bio-32.explanation_en: The A site is over the codon CCA, which the table assigns to Pro. The incoming tRNA must base-pair antiparallel with CCA, so its anticodon is 3'-GGU-5', and it carries Pro. The ribosome catalyzes a peptide bond that transfers Met from the P-site tRNA onto Pro, so the Met-Pro chain ends up on the A-site tRNA. The option with the anticodon identical to the codon is wrong because tRNA anticodons are complementary, not identical, to the codon. The option with the chain staying on the P-site tRNA is wrong because the chain is moved to the A-site tRNA, which then shifts to the P site at translocation. The option with Val is wrong because the A site reads CCA, not the downstream GUU codon.

s3-bio-33.stem: A biotechnology startup is deciding whether to invest in a process that reprograms cells from one specialized type into another. A scientist on the team claims: "Liver cells and pancreatic beta cells from the same mouse are different because they differ in expression of genes, not because they have different genes." Which statement uses the data in the table to best support this claim?

stimulus.description: Table of gene copy number per cell and mRNA abundance for three genes in two cell types from the same mouse.

columns: Copies per cell: pancreatic beta cell
mRNA (reads per million): pancreatic beta cell
data.units: copies per diploid cell; reads per million

options.text: Each gene has two copies in both cell types, showing that all genes are transcribed at equal rates in every cell of the mouse.
options.why: Misconception: equal gene copies imply equal transcription; contradicted by the mRNA data.

options.text: The actin gene has similar mRNA levels in both cell types, showing that actin is the only gene both cell types contain.
options.why: Misconception: similar expression of a housekeeping gene means only that gene is shared; ignores copy number data showing all three genes are present in both.

options.text: Albumin mRNA is high in liver cells and insulin mRNA is high in beta cells, showing that each cell type lost the other's gene.
options.why: Misconception: low mRNA means the gene was deleted; confuses lack of expression with lack of the gene, contradicted by 2 copies.

options.text: Each gene has two copies in both cell types, but the albumin and insulin mRNA levels differ greatly between the cell types.
options.why: Correct: equal copy number shows same genetic content; very different mRNA for albumin and insulin shows differential expression.

s3-bio-33.explanation_en: The claim has two parts: the cells have the same genes, and they differ in expression. Equal copy numbers (2 per cell for all three genes) show the same genetic content, and the strongly different albumin (4800 vs 3) and insulin (2 vs 5200) mRNA levels show differential expression. The option claiming actin is the only shared gene ignores that albumin and insulin genes are present in both cell types. The option claiming gene loss is wrong because low mRNA reflects reduced transcription, and both cell types still carry 2 copies. The option claiming equal transcription is contradicted by the mRNA data, since equal copy number does not mean equal expression.

s3-bio-34.stem: A student claims: "Cell types P, Q, and R differ in function because they use different subsets of the same set of genes." Which statement uses evidence from the table to best support this claim?

stimulus.description: Table of DNA detection and mRNA detection for six genes in three cell types (P, Q, R) isolated from one multicellular organism. 1 = detected, 0 = not detected.

data.notes: Binary detection data; all three cell types were taken from the same individual, derived from one zygote.

options.text: Cell type P has mRNA for g2 and g5 while cell type R has mRNA for g4, which shows that P and R contain different DNA sequences.
options.why: Misconception that different mRNA implies different DNA; the DNA columns are identical across P, Q, and R.

options.text: Gene g1 is detected as both DNA and mRNA in all three cell types, which shows that every gene in the genome is transcribed in every cell type.
options.why: Overgeneralizes from one constitutively expressed gene to all genes; g2 through g6 are not transcribed in every cell type, so the conclusion contradicts the data.

options.text: Gene g6 is detected as DNA but not as mRNA in any cell type, which shows that g6 was lost from the genome during specialization.
options.why: Misconception that unexpressed genes are lost or deleted; the DNA columns show g6 is present in all three cell types.

options.text: All six genes are detected as DNA in all three cell types, but only g1 is transcribed in all three; g2, g3, g4, and g5 are transcribed in some cell types and not others.
options.why: Correct: identical DNA content (all 1s) combined with cell-type-specific mRNA patterns directly supports differential expression of the same genome.

s3-bio-34.explanation_en: The claim is that the cell types use different subsets of the same genes. The DNA columns show every gene present in every cell type, so gene content is the same. The mRNA columns differ: g1 is transcribed everywhere, while g2, g3, g4, and g5 appear in only some cell types. Identical genomes with different transcription patterns support differential gene expression as the basis of specialization, which is what the correct option states. The option claiming all genes are transcribed everywhere is wrong because g2 through g6 are not transcribed in every cell type; one gene cannot represent the whole genome. The option claiming g6 was lost is wrong because the table shows g6 DNA is detected in all three cell types, so a lack of mRNA means the gene is not expressed, not deleted. The option claiming P and R have different DNA is wrong because the DNA columns are identical; different mRNA reflects different expression, not different sequence.

s3-bio-35.stem: A sports-genetics lab amplifies a 600 bp region of a muscle-fiber gene by PCR and cuts the product with a restriction enzyme, as shown in the table. Which conclusion about the athletes' alleles is best supported by the data, and why?

stimulus.description: Table of restriction fragment sizes (bp) observed on a gel after cutting a 600 bp PCR product from three athletes with the same enzyme.

data.title: Fragments produced by digesting a 600 bp PCR product of a muscle-fiber gene with one restriction enzyme
data.notes: Each athlete has two copies of the gene; the PCR primers amplify the same 600 bp region from both copies. Gel fragments are listed in descending size. The enzyme cuts only at its recognition sequence. Fragments of 70 bp and 130 bp together equal 200 bp.

options.text: Athlete 1 carries two alleles with the extra cut site, because the undigested 600 bp product was cut into two shorter fragments.
options.why: Misconception: treats any cutting as evidence of the variant site. The 400+200 pattern is one cut at the shared site, i.e., the allele without the extra site, so Athlete 1 is homozygous for that allele.

options.text: Athlete 3 carries one allele with the extra cut site and one without it, because the 400 bp fragment appears and the 200 bp fragment is absent.
options.why: Misconception: assumes missing a band means heterozygous. Athlete 3 shows only 400, 130, 70, so no allele lacks the extra site; the athlete is homozygous for the extra-site allele.

options.text: Athlete 2 carries one allele with the extra cut site and one without it, because both the 200 bp fragment and the 130 bp and 70 bp fragments appear.
options.why: Correct. Fragments of both the uncut-at-site pattern (400+200) and the extra-site pattern (400+130+70) are present, so the athlete has one allele of each type (heterozygous); the fragments sum to 600 per allele.

options.text: Athlete 2 carries a duplicated gene region, because the total of the fragment sizes exceeds the 600 bp size of the PCR product.
options.why: Misconception: adds the fragments from two alleles as if from one DNA molecule. The 600 bp total applies to each allele separately, so the larger sum reflects two different alleles, not a duplication.

s3-bio-35.explanation_en: The 600 bp product is cut once at a shared site into 400 + 200 bp. One allele has an additional site inside the 200 bp piece, giving 130 + 70 bp, so that allele yields 400 + 130 + 70 bp. Athlete 2 shows the 200 bp fragment (allele without the extra site) and the 130 and 70 bp fragments (allele with the extra site), so the athlete has one of each allele and is heterozygous. This shows how restriction digestion of PCR products distinguishes alleles by differences in DNA sequence. The option claiming Athlete 3 is heterozygous is wrong because Athlete 3 has no 200 bp fragment, which means both copies carry the extra site. The option claiming Athlete 1 has two extra-site alleles is wrong because Athlete 1's fragments match a single cut at the shared site only, which means neither copy carries the extra site. The duplication option is wrong because each allele's fragments sum to 600 bp, and the combined total from two alleles is expected to be larger than 600 bp in a heterozygote.

s3-bio-36.stem: Sequence differences were measured for a shared gene in five taxa (table). Assume differences accumulate at a constant rate and that Z is an outgroup to the other four taxa. Before taxon V was sequenced, the data for W, X, Y and Z supported a tree in which W and X are sister taxa, Y is their next closest relative, and Z is the outgroup. Which prediction best describes how adding the data for V changes this tree?

stimulus.description: Pairwise sequence differences (per 100 aligned sites) among five taxa for a shared gene.

data.title: Pairwise sequence differences per 100 aligned sites
data.note: Z is known to be an outgroup to W, X, Y and V. Assume a constant rate of change.

options.text: V joins the W and X clade as a third sister taxon, because V differs equally from W and from X.
options.why: Misconception: equal distances to W and X imply V belongs inside the W+X group; ignores that Y-W and Y-X are also 12 and that V is much closer to Y.

options.text: V and Y form a clade that shares a more recent common ancestor with each other than with W or X.
options.why: Correct: V-Y (6) is the smallest distance involving V, and V is equally distant (12) from W and X, as Y is, so V and Y share a recent ancestor and together are sister to W+X.

options.text: V branches off before all other taxa, because it has differences with every other taxon.
options.why: Misconception: any taxon that differs from all others must be basal; confuses having differences with being the most divergent.

options.text: V and Z form a clade, because both differ from W, X and Y by the same amount of 20 sites.
options.why: Misconception: equal large distances indicate shared ancestry; V-Z is 20 only because Z is the outgroup, and shared differences from an outgroup are not shared derived similarity.

s3-bio-36.explanation_en: The smallest difference involving V is with Y (6 per 100 sites), so V and Y share the most recent common ancestor of any pair including V. V differs from W and X by 12, the same as Y does, so V and Y together are equally related to the W+X clade, making V+Y a clade that is sister to W+X, with Z still the outgroup. The tree that treats V as a third member of the W+X group fails because V is far closer to Y (6) than to W or X (12), and the W+X pair (4) is much closer than either is to V. The claim that V branches off first fails because V's distance to Z (20) is the largest, so Z, not V, is the earliest branch. The claim that V and Z form a clade fails because both being 20 from other taxa reflects Z's outgroup position; a clade requires a small distance between the two taxa, and V-Z is 20.
